findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the relationship between the new _field_contract.py symmetry registry and the existing conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES registry (orthogonal axes to cross-reference, or one derived from the other) so the change does not create a second drift-prone field registry.
evidence: Existing registry: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/conflict_resolver.py:28 `FIELD_CLASSES: dict[str, str] = {"status": "state", "assignee": "state", "priority": "state", "title": "state", "type": "state", "description": "additive", "comments": "additive", "labels": "set", "watchers": "set", "links": "set"}`

FIELD_CLASSES is live and consumed: differ.py:595 (`if field in conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES`), apply_handlers.py:307 (`conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES.get(field_name) == 'set'`), and scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh:1885/1914 (documents per-field sync policy from FIELD_CLASSES).

The plan text (Context, Approach) names only should_propagate_removal, the tag dedup, and _OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD as the scattered policy — it never mentions FIELD_CLASSES, so the reader cannot tell whether the two registries are intended to coexist, whether one should derive from the other, or whether the field universe/class taxonomy overlap is intentional.
findings.finding: The plan proposes a new field registry (_field_contract.py) enumerating reconciled fields by symmetry class without acknowledging the existing conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES registry, which already enumerates nearly the same field universe by a conflict-resolution class (state/additive/set).
scenarios: A future field is added and gets a symmetry class in _field_contract.py but is forgotten in FIELD_CLASSES (or vice-versa), reintroducing exactly the scattered-policy drift this ticket sets out to prevent — now across two registries instead of one.
A reviewer or new call site must guess which of the two field registries is authoritative for 'how field X syncs'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph to Approach (1) noting FIELD_CLASSES (state/additive/set conflict axis) vs the new symmetry axis (bidirectional-roundtrip/add-wins/one-way-gated), asserting they are orthogonal, and either cross-referencing them in the docstrings or having the coverage guard also assert the two registries agree on the shared field universe.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reclassify the status codec: either declare it 'bidirectional-roundtrip UNDER the rebar-status annotation-label channel' and assert the roundtrip through that lossless path (labels + workflow status together), or give status its own symmetry class with a lossy-workflow + annotation-recovery property — do NOT assert bare local<->jira status identity, which config.py proves cannot hold for blocked/cancelled/deleted/in_review.
evidence: Plan: 'roundtrip identity asserted ONLY for declared-bidirectional value codecs (status mapping, link inward/outward direction)'
config.py local_to_jira_status: blocked/in_progress -> 'In Progress'; closed/cancelled/deleted -> 'Done' (forward map non-injective)
config.py jira_to_local_status: 'In Progress' and 'In Review' both -> 'in_progress' (reverse map non-injective)

inbound_translate.py:127 _jira_status_to_local docstring: 'The forward map is non-injective ... blocked/cancelled are encoded losslessly via rebar-status: annotation labels — callers ... apply that override BEFORE consulting this workflow-status map'

config.py:52-60: 'This is NOT derivable from local_to_jira_status ... Deriving the reverse map by inverting local_to_jira_status ... imported In Progress as blocked and Done as cancelled — ticket robe-creek-zealot'
link_direction.py INVERSE_RELATION is a genuine involution (relates_to a fixed point), so the link half of the claim IS sound — the defect is specific to status
findings.finding: The plan classifies 'status mapping' as a declared-bidirectional value codec and asserts roundtrip identity on it, but the status codec is provably non-injective in both directions and is lossless only via the rebar-status: annotation-label channel the plan never models — so a status roundtrip-identity property cannot hold as specified.
findings.location: Approach step (2) and Acceptance Criteria line 3 ('Roundtrip identity asserted only for declared-bidirectional codecs')
scenarios: A local ticket in status 'blocked' round-trips local->jira ('In Progress')->local ('in_progress') != 'blocked' — the identity property fails unless annotation labels are consulted
Jira 'In Review' round-trips to 'in_progress' then back to 'In Progress' != 'In Review'
'cancelled'/'deleted' both collapse to 'Done' and cannot be recovered from workflow status alone
findings.suggested_fix: Split status into (a) the lossy workflow-status map and (b) the rebar-status annotation-label channel that carries the lost states; assert roundtrip identity on the COMBINED codec (annotation-label-aware, matching _jira_status_to_local's documented caller contract), not on the workflow map alone.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the coverage guard enumerates 'handled fields' (introspect inbound_differ/apply_inbound_records vs. a maintained list) so the deletion mutation genuinely fails collection and a new undeclared field breaks the build.
evidence: "the test module enumerates the reconciled fields handled by inbound_differ/apply_inbound_records and fails collection if any handled field lacks a registry entry"
"Coverage guard fails collection for a handled-but-undeclared field (proven by the deletion mutation)."
ABSENCE: no statement of how 'handled fields' are discovered (code introspection vs. a static list)
findings.finding: The coverage guard's source of truth for 'reconciled fields handled by the differ/apply path' is unspecified: the plan does not say whether the guard independently introspects inbound_differ/apply_inbound_records or reads a separate maintained list. If it reads a hand-maintained list rather than deriving handled fields from the actual code path, the deletion mutation could pass (removing both the registry entry and its list entry) without failing collection, defeating AC#2.
findings.location: Approach (2) coverage guard; Acceptance Criteria line 2
scenarios: A new field is added to the differ without a registry entry but the guard's list isn't updated — build stays green, defeating the guard's purpose
Deletion mutation removes a registry entry but the guard derives handled fields from the same registry, so collection never fails
findings.suggested_fix: State that the guard derives the handled-field set from the differ/apply code (e.g., by inspecting the field-canonicalization map / dispatch table) rather than from the registry, so an undeclared handled field is detectable independently.
